questions.q: A woman has a positive pregnancy test shortly after implantation. Which hormone secreted by trophoblastic tissue maintains the corpus luteum during early pregnancy?
questions.explain: Syncytiotrophoblast secretes hCG, which acts on LH receptors to maintain the corpus luteum. The corpus luteum continues progesterone secretion until placental steroid production is sufficient.

questions.q: During labour, cervical stretch increases uterine contractions, which in turn produce further cervical stretch. Which feedback pattern does this illustrate?
questions.explain: Cervical stretch stimulates neuroendocrine oxytocin release and strengthens uterine contractions. Stronger contractions increase cervical stretch, reinforcing the response until delivery interrupts the cycle.

questions.q: Which hormone produced by the placenta is important for maintaining the maternal endometrium and reducing uterine contractility during pregnancy?
questions.explain: Placental progesterone maintains the decidualised endometrium and helps maintain uterine quiescence during pregnancy.

questions.q: Which feature of the placenta permits efficient exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between maternal and fetal blood without their normal direct mixing?
options: A thin placental barrier with closely apposed maternal and fetal circulations
Active pumping of fetal blood into maternal arteries
questions.explain: Maternal blood bathes chorionic villi while fetal capillaries lie within them. Gases diffuse across the placental barrier; the two blood supplies normally remain separate.

questions.q: Which hormone is chiefly responsible for milk synthesis by mammary alveolar epithelial cells after delivery?
questions.explain: Prolactin stimulates milk synthesis. Oxytocin causes myoepithelial contraction and milk ejection; the fall in placental progesterone after delivery permits copious milk production.
